newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans up sharply on exports, harvest delay.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans up sharply on exports, harvest delay.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were sharply higher with the May contract in fast dealings on USDA export inspections data and on talk that rains in Brazil would delay the soybean harvest, traders said.
USDA Tuesday morning pegged weekly U.S. export inspections at roughly 35 million bushels, above trade expectations for 20 million to 24 million bushels.

Traders also noted rains fell in Brazil over the weekend which prompted talk of delays in the harvest of early-cycle soybean crops. Rains were set to continue in the southern growing regions through Thursday, meteorologists said.
Soybeans also drew strength from a rally in corn futures tied to Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report.
Floor traders said funds were active buyers of soybeans, corn and wheat.
At 1009 CST, soybeans were four to 11 cents per bushel higher with March up 11 at $7.72.
